question: Does coupling forward torso sliding with opposing limb-contact sliding admit and sustain model progress while preserving force-direction, normal-contact, floor and joint constraints?

population.selection: Only original R10AP partial step1 / semantic step513. All later states are counterfactual and never native observations.
population.coverage: R10AW found tangential limb anchoring prevents forward motion, but its omissions lacked force/motion consistency. This distinct model enumerates physically labeled contact modes with opposing friction instead of adopting any omitted guard.

algorithm.mode_encoding: 0 inactive,1 sticking,2 sliding in original forward dominant sector,3 sliding in the opposing sector. The first two original contacts are torso points and allow0/2, at least one active. Each of five original limb contacts allows0/1/3. Enumerate itertools.product lexicographically, skipping both-torso-inactive:729 modes.
algorithm.original_mode_reproduction: The96 modes without state3 exactly reproduce R10AV eligible subset force feasibility and refusal, and first progress objective within1e-10.
algorithm.friction: Retain R10AV mu1.8 inner diamond and original signed dominant horizontal axis. State2 uses the forward sector and its opposing extreme force; state3 uses the reverse sector and reverse extreme force. State1 keeps the full sticking friction diamond. State0 contributes no force. Each contact has its own mode; contacts on the same body still share body kinematics.
algorithm.motion: State1 fixes xyz; state2/3 fixes normal height and constrains signed tangent motion to its designated maximum-dissipation sector. Retain all original-marker non-descent,24 floor witnesses, coordinate rate bounds,0.02-rad nonworsening headroom, and global original anchor/height/floor guards. No contact creation or floor removal.
algorithm.objective: First maximize torso-origin progress along the original horizontal heading. Then within1e-10 m of the optimum minimize sum(abs(delta_i)/maximum_i) over all14 coordinates using an epigraph LP. No arbitrary movement of unconstrained limbs is intentionally selected.
algorithm.finite_check: Mixed contact projection at most10 Newton corrections, four nonzero sample fractions and11 dyadic scales as in R10AS. Require forward torso progress>1e-9*fraction, every selected sliding signed dominant displacement between successive nodes>1e-12 m, and all geometry/sector residuals<=1e-9. Re-solve the sliding-force model at every admitted node. Check force dot segment displacement against the friction-diamond minimum within1e-9 J.
algorithm.selection: Choose the admitted entry mode with greatest finite forward torso progress, lower lexicographic mode_id wins ties. Keep that mode fixed for at most600 propagated model steps; no re-selection after exposure. Preserve all rejected entry modes and path refusals.
algorithm.termination: First model refusal, all-foot-cap COM hull gap<=1e-6 m, or600 admitted model steps. Preserve every attempted step, rejected scale, certificate and rebase. Hull inclusion is geometric only.
algorithm.no_tuning: No friction, cap, objective, mode, bound or interpretation changes after exposure.

checks: 36 manufactured controls:17 geometry/Jacobian,12 sliding-sector/drive/drag,7 coupled-mode/sign/enumeration controls.
Reproduce all96 predecessor mode outcomes before claiming completion of the survey.
All force and two-stage motion LPs retain checked primal/dual certificates; finite samples check maximum-dissipation displacement work for each sliding contact independently.
Rebase identity and global geometry guards prevent accumulated anchor or floor changes.
Cold-process exact reproduction of full survey and selected path.

research_sources.use: Coulomb friction, maximum dissipation, polyhedral friction and the distinction between contact models and actual dynamics.

limitations: Quasistatic and sampled-model evidence only. Opposing signed slide sectors are finite modes, not arbitrary Coulomb contact coverage. The authored coefficient is assumed for sliding, not native-calibrated. No inertial transition, continuous collision, contact acquisition, controller realization or dynamic success is proven. Original contact/callback staging, penetration and moving-entry limitations remain. Selection is of a model mode only.
